column1: # Plain-words reasons for failures, shown beside a failure only while it matches. counted: no marks
# failures that say nothing about the program: tests that drive another program instead of wkhtmltopdf, or a
# test in which the program never ran; they are shown, and not counted for or against anyone.

column5: Pictures from loremflickr.com: the test pages load pictures from loremflickr.com, which now answers with an error, and wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6 stops when a picture does not load.

Google's “Too Many Requests” page: these tests convert google.com, and Google answered this machine's requests with that page instead, so the program stopped with an error, as wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6 does when a page does not load. Each program runs on its own machine, and Google refuses some machines and not others.

Chrome, not wkhtmltopdf: the library's tests of its Chrome option drive Google Chrome through its own Node helper, and on these machines they mostly do not finish within ExUnit's one-minute limit; they are shown, and not counted.

A virtual display that did not start: the library starts the program inside a virtual display (xvfb-run), which failed to start on this machine, so the program never ran in this test; it is shown, and not counted.
A footer with missing files: the test footer loads a script and a picture that do not exist, and wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6 stops with an error on that.
No Chrome on ARM64: these tests open the demo application in Google Chrome through Selenium, which finds no Chrome on GitHub's ARM64 machines; they fail whichever program is installed.
